newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Police ponder gang link in Budapest shooting.
newsitem.headline: Police ponder gang link in Budapest shooting.

text.p: A Hungarian businessman has been shot and seriously wounded in what police said on Thursday could be the latest in a series of attacks blamed on a gangland turf war.
"It would be irresponsible to exclude such a possibility," a National Police spokesman told Reuters.

Pal Totka, 39, a former middleweight national boxing champion and restaurant owner, was shot in the chest, arms and hands on Wednesday night in front of his garage in a suburban residential district outside the Hungarian capital.
Totka, a father of two, underwent emergency surgery and doctors said he would survive.
The shooting comes after a series of unsolved attacks in Hungary's capital.
Jozsef Prisztas, a well-known figure in Budapest's underworld, was shot dead on November 1 at point-blank range. A prominent racehorse owner was seriously wounded two weeks later.
Several hand grenades have been exploded during the last three months outside night clubs, injuring no one but causing extensive damage in some cases.
National and Budapest police have recently beefed up the task force working on the cases to 160 officers from the previous 130, but have not yet put an end to the violence.
